newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets tax for small firms. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets tax for small firms. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline to delete reference to 7.5 pct)
Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Tuesday signed a decree setting a new single tax for small firms of 5.0-7.0 percent, officials said.
Under the new system, companies with turnover of up to 120,000 reais a year will pay a unified-tax and employer contribution rate of 5.0 percent of turnover.
The tax increases on a sliding scale to 7.0 percent for companies with annual turnover of up to 720,000 reais a year.

The government will also allow the renegotiation of debt owed by the small business sector to private and federal banks over the next 72 months. Only firms in the process of renegotiating debt or whose tax payments are in order will qualify for the new tax bracket.

Everardo Maciel, head of the Internal Revenue Service, said the unified tax system would simplify payment procedures for small companies and help the government tackle tax evasion by the informal sector.
Cardoso said the measures were "an important part" of the government's plans to reform the tax system as a whole.
But he said further simplification of the system was necessary.
"What's being done today is a tax revolution," said Joseph Couri, president of the Sao Paulo State Small Industries Union.
Brasilia began negotiating new tax rules for small firms after the Senate approved a bill that would have exempted them from tax altogether on turnover of up to 204,000 reais a year.
Finance Ministry officials warned the bill, if approved in the Chamber of Deputies, would have cost 4.0 billion reais in lost tax revenue.
